nodes.label: Tokenless single-owner identity model
nodes.rationale: The app is a local-first, single-user desktop-style app; backend runs on localhost:8000 serving one owner. current_user resolves the seeded owner (first users row) instead of per-request auth. Google OAuth links User to GoogleToken by email match, not FK, which is acceptable for single-owner; revisit before any hosted deployment.

nodes.label: Secrets at rest policy (local-only)
nodes.rationale: Local-first threat model: the SQLite DB file is the encryption boundary for Google OAuth refresh tokens; AI provider keys live in git-ignored backend/app/data/ai_providers.json. Acceptable only for single-user localhost deployment; encrypt token columns and move keys before any cloud/hosted deployment.

nodes.label: Dynamic-data rule (no static/mock/hardcoded data)
nodes.rationale: Fix every workflow defect without changing current UI/UX: same components, styles, layout. The only change allowed is removing static/mock/hardcoded data so every datum is fetched live from Second Brain / DB via API (useEffect -> endpoints.* subscribed to the listed KB source), reusing existing SkeletonCard/EmptyState patterns.

nodes.label: Destructive-action confirm policy (one owner: confirmDelete)
nodes.rationale: Message phrasing ('Delete X? This cannot be undone.') is owned by frontend/src/utils/confirm.ts confirmDelete() helper, not call sites, so wording or a styled dialog can be changed in exactly one file. Confirmations with bespoke non-delete explanations (KB reindex/merge/restore) are deliberately kept inline as one-off policies.

nodes.label: Seed data ownership rule (backend/app/seed/__init__.py)
nodes.rationale: Freshness decided once (fresh = user is None at top of seed_database); seed_vault_habits and seed_vault_demo run inside a single if fresh block so user deletions are never resurrected. LifeArea has exactly one seeder (seed_rpg_additions); the weaker satisfaction-only seeder in seed_full was deleted, not delete-then-reseed.

nodes.label: Presentation affordance (click affordance on the Link, not the wrapper div)
nodes.rationale: Click affordance (cursor: pointer) lives on the element that navigates (the <Link>), not the wrapper div, so Dashboard course cards no longer carry a misleading cursor: pointer on a non-interactive container.

nodes.label: F1: KbDocument god object (accepted by design)
nodes.rationale: KbDocument facets (identity/content/metadata/processing-state/versioning-dedupe) are documented in models/kb/document.py. Schema split rejected: no alembic, SQLite + create_all only, and 225+ importers depend on the flat surface. KbDocument is the currency of the app, not random accumulation; revisit if a migration tool is adopted.

nodes.label: F2: services/kb flat 70-file directory (partially done, deferred)
nodes.rationale: metadata/ sub-package extracted (core.py, frontmatter.py) as the template. Full reorg (core/pipeline/learning/automation/retrieval/metadata/shared) deferred by owner decision 2026-09-13 to avoid conflicting with concurrent in-flight work; apply incrementally, one group per feature touch.

nodes.label: F3: routers/kb_* 1:1 mirror with PEP 562 lazy imports
nodes.rationale: Router-per-service mirror pattern is idiomatic FastAPI; deferred as low priority. router __init__.py now uses PEP 562 lazy imports so the imports block is no longer a sync burden; merging kb_graph/kb_edges remains optional cleanup.

nodes.label: F4: course monolith decomposition (frontmatter.py + course_content_topics.py)
nodes.rationale: Frontmatter parsing moved to services/kb/metadata/frontmatter.py (pure functions). Topic tree + document resolution moved to services/course_content_topics.py with shared resolve_course_document_ids(); course_documents() and course_document_count() no longer duplicate the 3-path resolution. course_content.py is a 210-line aggregate.

nodes.label: F5: event-driven post-ingest hook registry in pipeline.py
nodes.rationale: pipeline.py no longer inlines feature calls: register_post_ingest() + run_post_ingest_hooks() provide an event-driven registry so daily-note tag, citation parse, and quality recompute are decoupled from ingest.

nodes.label: Code Audit Report — Cortex Productivity App (2026-09-11)
Audit F1: KbDocument god object spanning 3 layers
nodes.rationale: KbDocument (models/kb/document.py:24) is imported by 225+ services, 40+ routers, 20+ test files; any change risks cascading breakage. The god-object label is architecturally legitimate: KbDocument is the currency of the app. Risk is long parameter lists in service-layer functions; consider a DocumentHandle (id + path + owner only).

nodes.label: Audit F2: circular dependency risk in routers/__init__.py
nodes.rationale: routers/__init__.py imports auth_google, classroom, gmail, calendar at module load; importing * from routers downstream pulls those routers eagerly with heavy OAuth/Google API client dependencies. Recommendation: make __init__ imports lazy (registry pattern).

Student Life OS
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive single-user web app combining academic management, life productivity, RPG gamification, knowledge management (Second Brain), and AI-powered features.

nodes.label: Second Brain Vault Integration
nodes.rationale: KB engine is a custom pipeline (scan, chunk, embed, index, search) built in-house rather than external KB tooling; covers vault sources, document indexing, knowledge graph, auto-subject detection, course derivation, hybrid search, and RAG tutor.

nodes.label: Single-User Tokenless Design
nodes.rationale: Single-user app: no authentication needed, tokenless by design. User ID 1 is hardcoded throughout.

nodes.label: Offline-First AI Fallbacks
nodes.rationale: Every AI feature falls back to deterministic local generators so the app keeps working when no AI provider is reachable.

nodes.label: ProfileContext as Sole Shared State
nodes.rationale: No global state library by design; all state lives in component-level useState and ProfileContext is the only shared context (user profile, theme). Data fetching is per-component via useEffect with no request deduplication and no caching layer.

nodes.label: Typed Endpoints Object (api layer)
nodes.rationale: api.ts (4500+ lines) exposes a generic request() wrapper, api get/post/put/patch/del methods, 100+ type interfaces, and an endpoints object organized by feature module (courses, tasks, kb, ai, vault, fitness, rpg, search).

nodes.label: Silent Error Swallowing (.catch(() => {}))
nodes.rationale: .catch(() => {}) is used throughout the frontend, silently swallowing API errors so users see empty pages with no indication of failure.

nodes.label: Second Brain KB Pipeline (scan, chunk, embed, index, search)
nodes.rationale: Pipeline: KB watcher polls every 30s, scanner finds new/changed files, parser converts markdown to structure, chunker makes 1200-char chunks with 150 overlap, embedder produces 384-dim fastembed ONNX vectors, then FTS5 index, vector store, knowledge graph, concepts, auto-subject detection, and auto-course sync from course:* tags.

nodes.label: AI Provider Registry with Fallback Chain
nodes.rationale: Registry in app/data/ai_providers.json supports multiple providers (Ollama, OpenAI, etc.), an AI_MODELS_FALLBACK chain, per-feature budgets (summary_daily_limit, embeddings_daily_limit), a cache layer (600s TTL), and deterministic fallbacks when offline.

nodes.label: Column Migration Sprawl (30+ ALTER TABLE)
nodes.rationale: 30+ ALTER TABLE statements accumulated in database.py instead of a proper migration system, keeping the 40+ table schema current by patching columns at startup.

nodes.label: KB Router Explosion (50+ routers)
nodes.rationale: 50+ individual FastAPI routers exist for KB features (kb_sources, kb_documents, kb_search, kb_graph, kb_tutor, etc.) on top of 100+ service modules in services/kb/.

nodes.label: N+1 Query Pattern (VaultDashboard heatmaps and project summaries)
nodes.rationale: VaultDashboard loads one heatmap API call per habit and one summary call per project, causing excessive API traffic with many habits/projects.

nodes.label: Hybrid Search (FTS5 keyword + vector + RRF fusion)
nodes.rationale: kb/search.py runs FTS5 keyword search and vector similarity search, fuses them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion when mode=hybrid, and feeds a RAG pipeline (rewrite, retrieve, rerank, verify).

nodes.label: FSRS Spaced Repetition Algorithm
nodes.rationale: flashcard_srs.py applies the FSRS algorithm to graded cards, updating flashcards and inserting flashcard_schedules rows; flashcard XP earned during review is not persisted to the user profile.

nodes.label: No Real-Time Updates or Cross-Page Sync
nodes.rationale: No WebSocket/SSE for live data, no cross-page sync (completing a task on Dashboard does not update Tasks page), no background refresh, no optimistic updates, and the registered Service Worker is not functional.

nodes.label: No Request Cancellation on Navigation
nodes.rationale: Fast navigation can cause race conditions because in-flight fetches are never aborted; responses may update unmounted components.

nodes.label: Local Folder Scanning Connection Mechanism
nodes.rationale: The Second Brain connects via local folder scanning (KB_WATCH_ENABLED, 30s poll interval) over source folder paths like an Obsidian vault, not a cloud API; a deliberate local-first integration choice.

nodes.label: Dual Data Source Problem (DB notes vs KB documents)
nodes.rationale: Two disconnected note systems: traditional notes (DB notes table, Notes.tsx) and KB documents (KB pipeline, KnowledgeBase/VaultSearch/CourseDetail). A note created in Notes.tsx never appears in KB search and vice versa; DB notes are invisible to search, and Journal/Tasks/Habits/Grades are not synced into the vault either.

nodes.label: Course Derivation from course:* Tags
nodes.rationale: Vault documents tagged course:* are automatically synced into course records, deriving subjects from Second Brain content.

nodes.label: Auto-Subject Detection from Vault Folders
nodes.rationale: Subject folders in the vault are auto-detected and surfaced as subjects/domains without manual configuration.

nodes.label: Idempotent Append-Only Seed System
nodes.rationale: Seed data is demo/first-boot data, not fake production data: it runs only when no user exists (fresh = user is None), is idempotent and append-only so it will not duplicate on re-runs, and represents a realistic student's initial setup (1 user Alex Level 5 Wizard, 5 courses, 12 assignments, 14+ habits, 50+ habit logs, fitness hub, RPG quests, etc.) that the user can delete.

nodes.label: Vault Habits Resurrection on Boot (seed_vault_habits)
nodes.rationale: seed_vault_habits re-seeds vault habits on every boot so user deletions are resurrected; seed_rpg_additions similarly re-seeds life areas when count < 4.

nodes.label: Missing Delete Confirmation Dialogs
nodes.rationale: Destructive actions (task, habit, note, flashcard deck, KB source deletion) call the API immediately on a single click with no confirmation, risking accidental permanent data loss.

nodes.label: Missing Loading and Error States
nodes.rationale: Pages render empty content (zeros, blank tables) while API calls are in-flight and stay empty forever on failure because .catch(() => {}) swallows all errors; no skeletons, no retry options.

nodes.label: Missing CRUD UI (tasks, habits, projects, schedule, missions, rewards)
nodes.rationale: Several pages are read-only views over backend CRUD that already exists: Tasks, HabitTracker, Projects, Schedule, LifeAreas, Exams, Missions, and Rewards pages lack create/edit/delete UI even though the backend endpoints exist.

nodes.label: AI Chat Lacks Conversation Persistence and Streaming
nodes.rationale: AIChat keeps history in component state only (lost when the chat closes) and waits for the full response instead of SSE streaming; no frontend rate limiting or budget display.

nodes.label: Four-Phase Fix Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: 99 defects classified 12 Critical / 23 High / 38 Medium / 26 Low, then sequenced: Phase 1 critical CRUD + error states + confirmations + vault habits resurrection fix; Phase 2 UX (loading states, empty states, dashboard links, DB notes to KB bridge); Phase 3 data consistency (AbortController, N+1 fixes, debounce, global API error handler); Phase 4 polish (optimistic updates, search debounce, settings persistence, periodic refresh). All phases pending at time of writing.

nodes.label: End-to-End Workflow Validation Methodology
nodes.rationale: Each workflow is validated by tracing the complete data flow (User Action -> UI -> State -> API -> Backend -> Database/Second Brain -> Response -> State Update -> UI) to verify data is genuinely dynamic; post-fix checks require npm build + vitest + pytest plus manual smoke tests of all critical workflows.
